subject: Procurement intake: security evidence request for Aperio Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Procurement intake: security evidence request for Aperio Health

Hi Marta / Aperio procurement team,

Thanks for moving quickly here — excited to get Aperio set up. Before we can finalize the paperwork and issue a PO, procurement here needs our standard evidence pack (SOC 2 Type II summary, recent pen test attestation, and ISO certs where applicable) plus a completed vendor setup form. To keep timelines tight, can you please: 

- Confirm whether Aperio requires a redlined SOW or standard PO terms
- Share your supplier security questionnaire (SSQ) and your PO template (if different from the attachment)
- Indicate the legal entity name and remit-to address for the PO

I’ve looped in Laura (procurement) to own vendor setup and Marissa (security) for the evidence QA. We can target a PO issuance next week if we get the documents by EOD Wednesday.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_type2_summary.pdf, redwood_pen_test_letter_2025.pdf (evidence packet — high level).

Next steps I propose: you send the SSQ + PO template; Laura will follow up with the vendor onboarding form and W-9 request; Marissa will confirm any redaction rules for security artifacts.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Marta — great to meet you over email. I’m Laura from Redwood procurement, taking point on vendor setup. 

I’ve attached our vendor onboarding form and W-9 link in case that speeds things up (we typically need a signed W-9 and the onboarding form filled out). We received Karthik’s high-level evidence packet — thank you — and that looks sufficient for an initial procurement review. For the SSQ we normally ask for either a completed questionnaire OR answers plus supporting evidence (SOC 2 summary and pen test letter are perfect).

What I will do now:
- Send our vendor onboarding form (DocuSign) to your vendor ops contact by EOD today
- Start the internal vendor code request once the onboarding form is returned
- Open a procurement ticket with the PO team tied to deal AP-2026-0042 so we can queue the PO once codes are issued

Two quick asks for your team:
1) If there are any contract redlines, please mark them in the PO template and return; major legal exceptions should be flagged by your counsel.
2) Confirm whether Aperio requires any additional compliance evidence (e.g., ISO 27001 certificate). If yes, please attach.

I’ve added links below to the shared evidence folder (read-only) where Karthik’s SOC 2 summary and pen-test letter are already uploaded. I’ll follow up with the DocuSign onboarding link.

Thanks — Laura Bennett
Procurement Manager, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Dec 20, 2026 at 11:04 AM Marta Reynolds <marta.reynolds@aperio-health.com> wrote:
> Attached are our SSQ and PO template for your team to review: Aperio_Supplier_Security_Questionnaire.pdf, Aperio_PO_Template.docx.

Thanks for sending these over, Marta. A couple of operational notes from the security side: 

- SOC 2 summary: we can provide the Type II report under an NDA if required; the redwood_soc2_type2_summary.pdf included should be enough for a procurement gating decision.
- Pen test letter: our latest attestation (redwood_pen_test_letter_2025.pdf) covers external infrastructure and public-facing interfaces. If your SSQ requires a vulnerability breakdown, let us know which sections you need redacted — we generally redact specific IP addresses and internal hostnames.
- ISO: Redwood is not ISO-certified at the org level; if Aperio needs evidence of specific controls (e.g., asset management, incident response), we can provide control descriptions mapped to SSQ items.

Timeline: if we get the signed onboarding form and your confirmed PO remit details today or tomorrow, we can hand the vendor code to procurement on Thursday and aim for a PO by Friday. If your legal needs a redlined contract review, please flag the clauses so our counsel can prioritize.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Security and Compliance, Redwood Inference
